hassio_confirm.title: Tesla Bridge app found
hassio_confirm.description: The app `{slug}` announced itself as a Tesla Bridge server. Continue to finish setting up Tesla Bridge with it.

manual_bridge.title: Connect to the Tesla Bridge server
manual_bridge.description: Home Assistant is not running on Home Assistant OS, so the app cannot be installed automatically. Run the Tesla Bridge container yourself and enter how to reach its internal API. The token is `api_token` in its `/data/state.json`.

configure_app.title: Public name and certificate
configure_app.description: Cars and Tesla reach your home through a free DuckDNS name. If you don't have one yet, sign in at {duckdns}, create a subdomain and copy your token. The app keeps the name pointed at your home and gets a Let's Encrypt certificate for it automatically.

data.lets_encrypt_accept_terms: I accept the Let's Encrypt Subscriber Agreement

network.title: Open two ports on your router
network.description:
Forward these TCP ports from the internet to Home Assistant at **{ip}**:

- public port **{key_port}** → {ip}:**{key_host_port}** (Tesla fetches your public key)
- public port **{telemetry_port}** → {ip}:**{telemetry_host_port}** (your cars stream to it)

Both must be plain TCP forwards (no reverse proxy). If your router supports UPnP, Tesla Bridge can create and maintain them for you.

{detail}

data.upnp: Let Tesla Bridge open the ports automatically (UPnP)

certificate_failed.title: No certificate yet
certificate_failed.description:
The app could not get a Let's Encrypt certificate for your DuckDNS name:

`{error}`

Check the DuckDNS name and token in the app's configuration, then submit to try again.

origin.title: Allow your DuckDNS name in your Tesla developer app
origin.description:
Open the [Tesla developer dashboard]({dashboard}), edit your application and make sure that:

- **Allowed Origin(s)** contains `{origin}`
- **Allowed Redirect URI(s)** contains `{redirect}`

Save, then continue to sign in to Tesla. Tesla Bridge reuses the client ID, secret and key of your Tesla Fleet integration when they exist.

register.title: Registering with Tesla

vehicles.title: Add the key to your cars
vehicles.description:
These cars don't trust Tesla Bridge's key yet: **{cars}**.

On your phone, scan the code with the camera app (or open {url}). The Tesla app opens and asks you to approve the key; stay near the car with Bluetooth on. Repeat for each car (select it in the Tesla app first), then submit.

telemetry.title: How much should the cars stream?
telemetry.description:
Tesla bills each streamed value: about $1 per 150,000, with a $10 monthly credit per account. Cars only send values that changed, and only while awake; parked, asleep cars send nothing. While driving or charging, a car typically sends:

- **Essential**: about {essential_signals} values an hour (≈ ${essential_month} a month for a car that drives or charges an hour a day)
- **Standard**: about {standard_signals} values an hour (≈ ${standard_month} a month)
- **Everything**: about {everything_signals} values an hour (≈ ${everything_month} a month)

Essential and Standard send location and speed at most every 10 seconds; Everything sends them every second. Each car gets a *Streaming cost this month* sensor. You can change this later under **Configure**.

push_result.title: Streaming configured
push_result.description:
{results}

Each car switches to streaming the next time it wakes up.

powerwall.title: Fast local Powerwall updates
powerwall.description: Tesla Bridge can read your Powerwall gateway directly every few seconds (and keep working when the internet is down). Enter its local IP address and the customer password: the last 5 characters of the password on the gateway's label. Imported from the Tesla Powerwall integration: {imported}.

data.skip: Skip; use Tesla's cloud data only

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to Tesla again
reauth_confirm.description: Tesla Bridge needs you to sign in to your Tesla account again.

adopt.title: Replace your old Tesla integrations
adopt.description: Found: {integrations}. Tesla Bridge can take over their entities. They keep their entity IDs, names, areas and history, so dashboards, automations and the Energy dashboard keep working. The old integrations are then disabled; delete them once you're happy.

data.adopt: Take over their entities and disable them

reconfigure_domain.title: Register the new DuckDNS name
reconfigure_domain.description:
The app now uses `{origin}` instead of `{old}`. Cars can only stream to a name registered with Tesla.

1. Open the [Tesla developer dashboard]({dashboard}) and add `{origin}` to your application's **Allowed Origin(s)**.
2. Make sure the router still forwards both ports and that {key_url} opens from the internet.
3. Submit. Tesla Bridge registers the name and sends every car a new streaming configuration.

{error}

reconfigure_bridge.title: Tesla Bridge server
reconfigure_bridge.description: Where Home Assistant reaches the Tesla Bridge container's internal API. The token is `api_token` in its `/data/state.json`.

reconfigure_powerwall.title: Powerwall gateway
reconfigure_powerwall.description: Change how Tesla Bridge reads your Powerwall gateway locally. The password is the last 5 characters of the password on the gateway's label.

init.description:
Tesla bills each streamed value: about $1 per 150,000, with a $10 monthly credit per account. Cars only send values that changed, and only while awake; parked, asleep cars send nothing. While driving or charging, a car typically sends:

- **Essential**: about {essential_signals} values an hour (≈ ${essential_month} a month for a car that drives or charges an hour a day)
- **Standard**: about {standard_signals} values an hour (≈ ${standard_month} a month)
- **Everything**: about {everything_signals} values an hour (≈ ${everything_month} a month)

Essential and Standard send location and speed at most every 10 seconds; Everything sends them every second. Each car gets a *Streaming cost this month* sensor.

api_cost_projected.name: Tesla API cost projected for this month

wake_up_timeout.message: The car did not wake up in time.

cable_lock_auto.message: The charge cable locks automatically when plugged in.

no_location.message: The car's location is not known yet.

bridge_unreachable.title: Tesla Bridge app not reachable
bridge_unreachable.description: Home Assistant cannot reach the Tesla Bridge app ({detail}), so cars cannot stream. Make sure the app is installed and running; this clears itself once it is reachable again.

powerwall_auth.title: Powerwall gateway rejected the password
powerwall_auth.description: Local Powerwall updates are off because the gateway rejected the customer password. Open Tesla Bridge in Settings → Devices & services, choose **Reconfigure** from its menu (then **Powerwall gateway**, if asked) and enter the last 5 characters of the password on the gateway's label.

missing_key.title: {name} doesn't have the Tesla Bridge key
missing_key.description: Tesla skipped {name} because the car does not trust Tesla Bridge's key yet. On your phone, open {url} near the car and approve the key in the Tesla app. Tesla Bridge checks every 10 minutes and configures streaming as soon as the key is approved.

bridge_auth.title: Tesla Bridge app rejected Home Assistant
bridge_auth.description: The Tesla Bridge app no longer accepts Home Assistant's access token, usually because it was reinstalled or its data was reset. Tesla Bridge picks up the new token by itself once the app has started and announced it. If this stays for more than a few minutes, restart the Tesla Bridge app.

bridge_auth_manual.title: Tesla Bridge server rejected Home Assistant
bridge_auth_manual.description: The Tesla Bridge container no longer accepts Home Assistant's API token, usually because its data was reset. Open Tesla Bridge in Settings → Devices & services, choose **Reconfigure** → **Tesla Bridge server address and token** and enter the `api_token` from the container's `/data/state.json`.

app_ports_disabled.title: Tesla Bridge app ports are turned off
app_ports_disabled.description: Port 443 or 8443 of the Tesla Bridge app is turned off in its Network settings, so Tesla and your cars cannot reach it (and UPnP leaves that port alone). Open Settings → Apps → Tesla Bridge → Configuration → Network, give both ports a host port and restart the app.

domain_changed.title: Tesla Bridge app uses a new DuckDNS name
domain_changed.description: The app now uses **{new}**, but Tesla Bridge is registered with Tesla for **{old}**, so your cars keep streaming to {old}. Open Tesla Bridge in Settings → Devices & services and choose **Reconfigure** → **Register the app's new DuckDNS name with Tesla**, or change the app's DuckDNS name back to {old}.

api_budget.title: Tesla API use may run past the free $10 credit
api_budget.description:
At its current rate, Tesla Bridge's use of Tesla's API comes to about **${projected}** a month (${spent} so far this month), mostly {top}. Above $10, Tesla turns off your developer app until next month and removes your cars' streaming setups; Tesla Bridge sends them again once Tesla allows it.

To use less, open Tesla Bridge in Settings → Devices & services, choose **Configure** and pick a lighter streaming preset. Your developer app's billing and usage page on developer.tesla.com shows what Tesla actually counted, including other integrations that use the same developer app.
